summary.text: An eight-year-old Senegalese boy with HbSS sickle cell anemia presented with over two years of chronic diarrhea and weight stagnation; he had multiple VOC with significant anemia episodes, leading to hydroxyurea. Mild intermittent transaminase/GGT elevation was seen on serial blood tests; hydroxyurea was ruled out as the cause of the GI symptoms. Abdominal pain, fever, tenesmus and vomiting were absent. Initially normal fecal calprotectin rose to 2600 µg/g in 6 months and occult blood was positive.

EGD was normal; colonoscopy showed pancolitis with erythematous mucosa, loss of vascularity and small ulcers, and biopsy confirmed chronic active colitis without crypt abscesses (the Figure 1 caption names ulcerative colitis, kept provisional). Initial improvement on 5-ASA and azathioprine was followed by failure of infliximab, adalimumab and an accelerated ustekinumab regimen; he is now on vedolizumab with a good response. Enterography and MRCP, done to exclude other GI complications, were normal. The Discussion attributes failure of initial UC management to overlap with ischemic colitis (not a diagnosis).

summary.text: A nine-year-old Senegalese girl with HbSS sickle cell anemia had four years of recurrent abdominal pain and poor weight gain with frequent ED visits for pain that resolved within hours. Persistent transaminase, bilirubin and GGT elevation contrasted with normal abdominal ultrasound, viral serologies and MRCP; celiac disease was ruled out. Positive anti-smooth muscle antibodies led to a liver biopsy that confirmed AIH (Figure 2 caption: mild lymphocytic infiltration, lobular inflammatory activity, focal hepatocyte necrosis).

She was treated with oral steroids followed by azathioprine and underwent an HLA-compatible bone marrow transplant, which the authors state cured both AIH and SCA. She has maintained normal liver enzymes and blood counts without further treatment.

summary.text: A 15-year-old Moroccan girl with HbSS sickle cell anemia and multiple admissions for hemolytic and vaso-occlusive crises had four years of persistent abdominal pain and constipation. Choledocholithiasis was diagnosed and managed with MRCP, laparoscopic cholecystectomy and ursodeoxycholic acid, but pain persisted with negative infectious stool studies. Examination showed a linear intergluteal fissure and hypertrophic anal papilla, and fecal calprotectin intermittently peaked at 1800 µg/g.

Endoscopic studies including capsule endoscopy and colonoscopy showed two small duodenal ulcers and non-necrotizing epithelioid granulomas in the perianal area, confirming Crohn disease. Oral budesonide followed by azathioprine achieved complete remission; she is currently on azathioprine 100 mg daily and remains asymptomatic.
